questions.question: The Preamble of the Indian Constitution was amended by which Constitutional Amendment Act?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment (1976) added the words 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' to the Preamble. It is the only amendment to the Preamble so far.

questions.question: Which of the following writs is issued to a public official to perform a duty they have failed to perform?
questions.explanation: Mandamus ('we command') is issued to a public official/body to perform a public duty. Habeas Corpus is against illegal detention; Certiorari transfers/quashes a case; Quo Warranto questions the legality of holding a public office.

questions.question: With reference to a Money Bill, which of the following statements is NOT correct?
options: It can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha
The Rajya Sabha can amend or reject it
It requires the prior recommendation of the President
The Speaker's decision on whether a bill is a Money Bill is final
questions.explanation: The Rajya Sabha cannot amend or reject a Money Bill — it can only make recommendations within 14 days, which the Lok Sabha may accept or reject.

questions.question: In which case did the Supreme Court hold that the 'Right to Privacy' is a Fundamental Right?
options: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
Justice K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India
S.R. Bommai v. Union of India
questions.explanation: In Puttaswamy (2017), a nine-judge bench unanimously held that the right to privacy is intrinsic to Article 21 and Part III of the Constitution.

questions.question: Which one of the following is NOT a discretionary power of the Governor?
options: Reserving a bill for the consideration of the President
Recommending President's Rule in the state
Appointing the Chief Minister when no party has a clear majority
Assenting to a Money Bill passed by the State Legislature
questions.explanation: Assent to a duly passed Money Bill is not a discretionary function. Reservation of bills, recommending Article 356, and CM appointment in a hung assembly are situational/discretionary powers.

questions.question: The Eleventh Schedule of the Constitution, added by the 73rd Amendment, contains how many subjects?
questions.explanation: The 11th Schedule lists 29 functional items for Panchayats. The 12th Schedule (74th Amendment) lists 18 items for Municipalities.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Election Commission of India:
1. It is a three-member body.
2. The Chief Election Commissioner can be removed in the same manner as a Supreme Court judge.
3. Election Commissioners can be removed by the President on the recommendation of the CEC.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.explanation: All three are correct. The ECI has a CEC and two ECs; the CEC has security of tenure like an SC judge (removal by special majority); ECs are removed by the President on the CEC's recommendation.

questions.question: Which part of the Constitution deals with Fundamental Duties?
questions.explanation: Part IVA (Article 51A) contains the 11 Fundamental Duties, added by the 42nd Amendment (10 duties) and the 86th Amendment, 2002 (11th duty — education of children aged 6–14).

questions.question: The 'Zero Hour' in Indian parliamentary practice:
options: Is mentioned in the Rules of Procedure of the Lok Sabha
Is an Indian innovation not found in the Rules of Procedure
Was borrowed from the British Parliament
Is presided over by the Vice President in both Houses
questions.explanation: Zero Hour (starting around 12 noon after Question Hour) is an Indian parliamentary innovation since 1962. It is not mentioned in the Rules of Procedure.

questions.question: Under which Article can the Supreme Court transfer a case from one High Court to another?
questions.explanation: Article 139A empowers the SC to transfer cases. Article 141 — SC law binding on all courts; Article 143 — advisory jurisdiction; Article 136 — special leave petition.
